name: uptime-kuma
one_liner: A self-hosted dashboard that pings your websites, servers, and APIs around the clock and alerts you the moment one goes down — like UptimeRobot, but free and running on your own server.
buyer: A freelance web developer or small digital agency managing uptime for a handful of client websites who doesn't want to pay per-site monitoring fees.
business_use_cases: A freelance developer self-hosts it once and monitors uptime for every client site from one dashboard, instead of paying for a monitoring tool per client.
A small hosting company bundles it as a free 'status page' perk for customers to differentiate from bigger, pricier hosts.
A managed-services shop offers 'we'll watch your site 24/7 and text you if it goes down' as a paid add-on built on this free tool.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a managed-hosting version with guaranteed uptime and SMS alerts, billed per site monitored
Sell setup-and-maintenance packages to small businesses who want monitoring but won't touch a server themselves

steal_this: Resell it as 'Website Watchdog' — host it once, monitor dozens of small-business client sites, and charge each client $10-20/month for alerts, since the underlying tool costs you nothing.
